bib.title: Unsupervised Dense Information Retrieval with Contrastive Learning

question: Can a dense retriever be trained with no supervision, using contrastive learning, to match BM25 and to serve as pre-training for supervised, few-shot and multilingual retrieval?
hypothesis: Contrastive learning with positive pairs built from a single document (random cropping) and many negatives (MoCo) yields unsupervised dense retrievers competitive with BM25.
contributions: Contrastive learning gives strong unsupervised retrievers, competitive with BM25 on Recall@100 on most of BEIR
In a few-shot setting the model benefits from few examples and beats transfer from MS MARCO
As pre-training before MS MARCO fine-tuning it gives strong BEIR performance
Ablations show cropping works better than the inverse Cloze task
A multilingual dense retriever (mContriever) trained with contrastive learning reaches state-of-the-art on Mr. TyDi Recall@100 and cross-lingual MKQA

method.summary: Contriever is a shared-weight BERT-base bi-encoder (mean-pooled last layer, dot-product score) trained with an InfoNCE loss on two random crops of the same document, with a MoCo momentum-encoder queue of negatives. It is evaluated unsupervised, after MS MARCO fine-tuning, few-shot, and in a multilingual variant (mContriever).
method.task: Document/passage retrieval (BEIR, NaturalQuestions, TriviaQA, Mr. TyDi, MKQA)

datasets.name: Wikipedia + CCNet (pre-training)
datasets.split: half of batches from each source
datasets.source: Wikipedia and CCNet (Wenzek et al., 2020); random pieces of text of 256 tokens
datasets.preprocessing: random cropping, span 5%-50% of document length, token deletion p=10%

datasets.name: BEIR
datasets.size: 18 datasets; 14 used in averages (3 excluded for licence, MS MARCO excluded from averages)

datasets.name: NaturalQuestions, TriviaQA (open domain)
datasets.split: test; collection = English Wikipedia dump of Dec. 20, 2018

datasets.name: SciFact / NFCorpus / FiQA (few-shot)
datasets.split: SciFact: 10% of train held out as dev, leaving 729 train samples

datasets.name: MKQA (cross-lingual)
datasets.source: Longpre et al. 2020; retrieval over English Wikipedia
datasets.preprocessing: unanswerable, yes/no and long-answer questions removed; queries and documents lowercased at evaluation

models.name: Contriever
models.architecture: BERT-base uncased bi-encoder, one shared encoder for query and document, mean pooling of last layer

models.name: BM25, DPR, ANCE, TAS-B, GenQ, ColBERT, Splade v2, REALM, SimCSE (RoBERTa large), CORA, mBERT/XLM-R + MS MARCO

training.objective: InfoNCE contrastive loss with temperature; MoCo queue of negatives with momentum-encoder keys (theta_k <- m theta_k + (1-m) theta_q)
training.optimizer: AdamW for pre-training; ASAM for English MS MARCO fine-tuning; AdamW for multilingual fine-tuning
training.lr: 5e-5 pre-training; 1e-5 MS MARCO fine-tuning (English and multilingual)
training.lr_schedule: mContriever pre-training: linear warmup then linear decay; multilingual fine-tuning: linear decay after warmup; English schedule not stated
training.warmup: mContriever pre-training 20,000 steps; multilingual fine-tuning 1000 steps
training.batch_size: 2,048 pre-training; 1024 MS MARCO fine-tuning (ablations: 2,048 pretrain on 32 GPUs, 512 fine-tune on 8 GPUs); few-shot 256; multilingual fine-tune 1024
training.steps: 500,000 pre-training (Contriever and mContriever); MS MARCO 20,000 steps for the first (random negative) model, then a second model with hard negatives (steps not stated); Mr. TyDi 20k; NQ 1k; ablations 200k pre-train, 20k fine-tune
training.epochs: few-shot: 500 epochs with early stopping on dev every 100 updates
training.seq_len: 256 tokens per document (crop spans 5%-50% of it)
training.hardware: ablations: 32 GPUs pre-training, 8 GPUs fine-tuning; GPU type not stated

other.finetune_negatives: in-batch, no MoCo; each query has gold doc and one negative (random in phase 1, hard negative 10% of the time in phase 2)
other.multilingual_temperature_no_pretrain: tau=1 for mBERT, 5 for XLM-R, chosen from {10,5,2,1,0.1,0.05}
other.NQ_finetune: reduced to 1k steps due to overfitting

inference.samples: not stated; single run per configuration, no seeds or variance reported
inference.retrieval: bi-encoder dot product over pre-encoded collection (FAISS cited); cross-encoder re-ranks top 100 for Ours+CE

metrics.name: nDCG@10
metrics.definition: ranking quality of top 10 retrieved documents; BEIR main metric

metrics.name: Recall@100
metrics.definition: recall of relevant documents in top 100; Trec-COVID uses capped Recall@100 per BEIR

metrics.name: top-k retrieval accuracy
metrics.definition: number of questions for which at least one of the top-k passages contains the answer (NQ, TriviaQA)

baselines: ICT and masked salient spans (Sachan et al. 2021)
eval.protocol: Single reported numbers per setting; no seeds, variance or significance tests. Averages exclude MS MARCO and (for 'w/o CQA') CQADupStack; 3 BEIR datasets excluded for licence.

availability.weights: pre-trained models released at the same repo

evidence.quote: queue of size 131,072, a momentum value of 0.9995 and a temperature of 0.05

limits: Unsupervised model loses to BM25 on nDCG@10 average and on Trec-COVID, Touche-2020
Authors say long documents (Touche-2020) are poorly supported by dense retrievers
MS MARCO fine-tuning is simple: no distillation and simple negative mining; authors expect more gains from adding those
No seeds, variance or significance tests reported; parameter count, compute, GPU type and wall clock not stated
Multilingual pre-training on more languages degrades performance
Unsupervised mContriever lags BM25 on MRR@100

samples independently two spans from a document to form a positive pair
